newsitem.title: USA: Great Western Q1 merger costs $33.7 mln.
newsitem.headline: Great Western Q1 merger costs $33.7 mln.

text.p: Great Western Financial Corp said Wednesday that net earnings for the first quarter were reduced by merger-related costs totalling $33.7 million.
Great Western has agreed to merge with Washington Mutual Inc and has rejected a takeover bid by H.F. Ahmanson and Co.

Great Western posted first quarter net income of $65.7 million, or $0.44 per share, versus $71.3 million, or $0.47 per share, a year earlier. It said operating income rose 25 percent, to $89.1 million or $0.61 a share.

The merger costs included investment banking, legal and consulting fees, and severance costs related to fourth quarter restructuring charges triggered effective February 25, 1997, on adoption of a severance plan for employees.

This increase to the restructuring accrual recorded in the 1996 fourth quarter was for severance charges which employees terminated after February 24, 1997, are entitled to under a change-in-control severance plan adopted on that date.
Net interest income totaled $338.2 million in the first quarter versus $352.3 million a year earlier.
Excluding the merger-related charge, noninterest expense totaled $244.7 million versus $267.1 million a year ago.
The drop in noninterest expense came from reduced salaries and benefits of $11.1 million, and a lower FDIC insurance premium of $11.6 million.
